dedupe_keys.name: discrete event simulation of post earthquake water system functional loss and restoration tomar burton mosleh lee

description: This model is the end-to-end simulation framework for post-earthquake functional loss and restoration of a water distribution system developed in Agam Tomar's 2020 UCLA dissertation and published in the Journal of Infrastructure Systems. It links seismic hazard characterisation, component damage assessment, hydraulic performance evaluation and network restoration modelling; the restoration step is a discrete-event simulation in which pipes, tanks and pumps go through events such as damage and inspection of variable duration, gated by crew availability and other events. The framework is validated on the 2014 South Napa earthquake and extended to a hypothetical scenario, then to stochastic event sets from the UCERF2 rupture forecast with active learning to cut the number of ground motion maps needed, and to Bayesian updating of recovery forecasts from real-time repair data. Outputs are probabilistic restoration curves with uncertainty bounds, outage maps over time and crew and material use. Coverage: one real network and event plus hypothetical cases. Access: the dissertation is a free PDF; code availability and language are not stated in the pages read, and the licence is not stated. Caveats: validation rests on a single earthquake and reconstructed repair data. It supports resilience and emergency response planning for water utilities, and relates to the Ann Arbor synthetic water distribution earthquake case study in the catalogue.
